<!-- pr-reviewer: 3fa2631c0f65cff2d18dacc8dd168ada2379e493 -->
**Needs changes before merge.** I reviewed only the three commits on top of #784 (c261f6fe, 28b5e682, 3fa2631c), trial-merged with `upstream/main` (merged cleanly).

### What looks good
- `march::shell_in` uses the same half-open bracket as `parity_of` (`c > z`): `(cm, ca]` for a top and `(ca, cm]` for a floor. So a mesh-only sign flip always has a crossing to read, and `Unreadable` is reachable only through a cut with no record. That matches the decision record.
- The broken-promise exits in both `refine` and `refine_down` return the last proven-air height. That over-reports material, which is the safe direction. `cut_downs` (a moved `cut_ups` bisection, which keeps the proven-inside side) puts the floor at or below the true cut top, so it errs safe as well.
- The bounded-tool refusal is still there: `cut_near(floor)` in `column_span`, and in `sliver` any claimed centre refuses when `bounded_cuts` is set. After this PR, the only thing that sets `bounded_cuts` is the tool's own flag (`field_turn.rs:143`).
- The pins catch real mutations. I changed `cn - d` to `cn - 0.5 * d` and 1 `field_floor` test plus 1 `carry_engine_agreement` test failed. I dropped the `d == 0.0` skip and 2 + 2 failed. I removed the level-facet branch in `plane_claim` and `a_level_facet_crosses_at_exactly_its_height` failed.
- No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside tests. All files are under 400 lines (`march_up.rs` is 130) and new modules carry a provenance line. No snapshot, golden or process-file changes. The body has `Changelog:` and ends with `Fixes #780`.

### Local results (merged with main, macOS, debug unless noted)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| sim lib | 69 passed (includes `solid_rest` 8 and the `field_turn` unit test) |
| sim `carry_engine_agreement` | 10 passed |
| sim `field_floor` | 10 passed |
| sim `field_carry` / `field_body` | 9 / 6 passed |
| sim `stock_backend_parity` | 13 passed |
| sim `stock_carry` / `stock_sim` / `stock_sdf` | 7 / 24 / 9 passed |
| sim `hidden_rest_banded` / `ridge_rest` / `scan_arc` | 5 (1 ignored) / 4 / 2 passed |
| sim, the other 16 suites in the quick plan | 152 passed, 0 failed |
| motion `posed_subtract` | 1 passed |
| app `stock_export` / `verify` / `setup_carry` / `carried_verify` / `rest_across_setups` | 2 / 21 (2 ignored) / 9 / 8 / 7 passed |
| app `stock_engine_agreement`, release `--ignored` | 3 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

### Requested before merge
1. **`march_up` under-reports a flipped floor where the cell probe is exactly 0, and lifting E2a's refusal exposes it** (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/march_up.rs:111-112`, with `field_turn.rs:143`).
   - **The shortcut.** `if phi == 0.0 { return ReadUp::Floor(z) }` copies `march`'s "the probe landed ON the surface" shortcut. But the probe's magnitude belongs to the cell, so `phi == 0` means the cell *centre* lies on a mesh plane, not that `z` does. The ascent returns whatever height it reached inside that cell.
   - **Scenario.** A plate `cube((0,0,-6.25),(20,12,0))` at cell 0.5, so the old floor -6.25 sits on a centre. Cut a flat r 2.0 slot along y 6 at z -5.8, then bake the flip `y -> -y, z -> -z`. At `column_span(10.25, -6.25)` the true material is [5.8, 6.25].
   - **What it reads.** This PR answers `Material { top: 6.4406, floor: 6.05 }`, so 0.25 of steel reads as air. The `floor: 6.05` comes from the `phi == 0` exit; I traced it locally. #784's head (80a79a15) answered `CutFromBelow` here.
   - **How widespread.** Across a sweep of plate floors {-6, -6.25, -6.1, -6.3, -5.9}, tops {0, 0.25, 0.1, -0.2} and slot depths from 0.5 below to 3 above the floor, 13 flipped configurations under-report the floor by 0.05 to 0.25. All have the floor on a centre (-6.25), and #784 refused every one of them by name.
   - **Fix.** Treat `phi == 0` as "this cell's centre is on a surface", not as a floor at `z`. Refine from the cell (`refine_down` from its centre), or answer `Unreadable`. Do the same for the `p == 0.0 => Floor(z_hi)` arm at `:120`.
   - **Pin.** Add a `field_floor` fixture with a stock plane on a cell centre: the slot above, flipped, with the floor within 1e-6 of 5.8. The cut-after-flip fixtures all use block planes on cell boundaries, so they never reach this exit.
   - **Until then,** keep E2a's `bounded_cuts` on a flipped bake. The answer to "can the interim refusal be lifted?" is not yet.

### Commit 3 (`solid_rest::plane_claim`) impact
- **Callers.** `column_crossings`, which feeds the field engine's `shell_crossings` (`field.rs:223`), and with it `march`, `march_up`, `column_span` and the march verdicts. Also `scan_hidden`, the hidden-rest scan behind `scan::hidden_rest`, through `plane_claim` and `crossings_from_claims` directly. `camcraft-app` only re-exports the module (`lib.rs:73`). The column engine's heightfield does not call it.
- **What moves.** Only a facet whose three z are equal, and only by the ulp the barycentric sum rounded. Pairing, `Open`/`Paired` and the 1e-9 level clusters are unchanged in practice.
- **Verdict at a point exactly on a level face.** `parity_of` counts `c > z`, so the law is half-open [floor, top).
  - On a level top face, a point exactly at the plane could read inside when the sum rounded up; now it always reads outside, which is the law.
  - On a level floor face, a point exactly at the plane could read outside when the sum rounded up; now it always reads inside, which means more material, the safe direction.
  - Either way the change is a zero-measure set brought into line with the stated law, not a flip on any open region.
- **Results.** `stock_engine_agreement` in release `--ignored` passed 3/3 on the merged tree. `hidden_rest_banded`, `ridge_rest`, `stock_sim` and `stock_sdf` are green.
- **Caveat (not blocking).** `crossings_from_claims` averages a level's claims (`sum / count`). With 3 or more claims of one off-lattice level at a shared vertex (5.1 + 5.1 + 5.1, then / 3), the mean can still miss `z` by an ulp. The pin's 21x21 grid includes the diagonal (2 claims, exact) but no vertex where 3 or more facets meet.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
- **A pre-existing defect on `main` (not caused by this PR).** `march`'s own `phi == 0.0 => Read::Top(z)` (`march.rs:241-242`) has the same flaw upright. On `cube((0,0,-6.25),(20,12,0))` with a flat slot at -6.0, `column_span(10.25, 6.25)` reads `Material { top: -6.25, floor: -6.25 }` where [-6.25, -6.0] stands. The same happens at #784's head, and `march` with that line is on `main` (it feeds `march_verdicts` and `columns`). The field engine is not the default, but this deserves its own issue, and the fix above should probably go in both marches.
- **Upright verdicts are not byte-identical for off-lattice floors.** That is expected from the shell-crossing read, but the body says the upright path is byte-identical. On a -6.3 floor, two configurations went from `Unreadable` to an exact read and one (slot at -6.25) went from a read to `Unreadable`. None under-reports.
- **Off-lattice plates still over-report their top by up to ~0.2.** For example, a 1.8..2.2 plate reads top 2.24 and a 2.0..2.25 plate reads 2.44. These come through the broken-promise path, because the probe's parity is taken at `z`, not at the cell centre. This is the safe direction and identical at #784's head; it is only a note against "exact to rounding".
- The PR title says `refactor`, while #780 is filed as a `feat` with enhancement labels. `Changelog: none` fits, since no shipped verdict changes; the type is for the merger to choose.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
